children: drew fresh attention Friday after Stifel lifted its price target to $530 from $450, while keeping a Hold rating.

The revised view follows meetings with Microsoft executives, with analyst Brad Reback pointing to broader adoption of Microsoft 365 Copilot as customers move from testing to wider deployments. Stifel also sees room for Azure to improve efficiency as the company expands its artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Reback said Microsoft is positioning Copilot for heavier usage in the second half of 2026. The analyst also cited rising engagement and increased customer interest in higher-priced Microsoft 365 offerings, which could support revenue per user.

Microsoft continues to support multiple large language models across Azure, GitHub and Copilot rather than relying on one model provider. That strategy could give the company more flexibility as AI workloads develop.
The higher target gives Microsoft a modest upside case, although Stifel's Hold rating signals a measured view.

title: Microsoft Stock Gets Jaw-Dropping Price Target Hike From Stifel
